why: Battery banks and material plots lacked native site feedback before placement. Copying a configured ground battery also omitted its inherited equipment condition.
change: New, copied and moved assets use the existing asynchronous native preview. Preview and commit share the same owned-object edit. Battery copies retain capacity, charge and any inherited condition/defer policy under their new battery identity. Moves retain identity and condition; timber copies retain phase, wetness and harvest/replant policies. External connections are not duplicated.
checks: All six asset tools have one native-eligible and one occupied site checked through ordinary controls, with rejected-click isolation and exact undo/redo. Configured battery and mature timber copy/move, native readiness, saved reload and history restoration pass with no page errors and completed bounded cleanup. Existing battery authoring/playtest and resource-site authoring/playtest regressions both exit 0, including drag movement, invalid draft repair, mapped extraction, conserved opening assets and exact checkpoints.
visual_review: Individually inspected the retained first successful allowed-stone and battery-copy captures, then the final blocked-stone capture from the same unchanged runtime sources. The stone-deposit overlay, ghost and written site reason are readable; the blocked footprint is warm red. Capture-only verifier changes added the blocked image for the final report.
limits: One eligible/occupied site per tool; configured copy/move coverage uses a battery and timber. Not every geology profile, cultivation state, resource type movement, riverbank/edge or maximum-entity combination. Existing playtest regressions validate opening assets, not a sustained gameplay/performance gate.
